title: WILDS: A Benchmark of in-the-Wild Distribution Shifts
mechanism: Splits defined by groups (hospital, camera, region). ID and OOD scores are reported separately through a standard loader and evaluator; ERM remains a strong baseline.
adaptation: Groups = module and source. Splits: ID test (seen modules), OOD-module test (E1, half-cut, scuffs), and leave-one-source-out (BMRK, SDLE). Report the worst-source score. The 11.9k/159k pool plays the role of WILDS-unlabeled (arXiv:2112.05090).
min_experiment: Re-score existing house and PF checkpoints per source and on E1. Decision: if the source-wise ranking of house vs PF differs from the pooled ranking, the worst-source score enters the headline.
prior_overlap: Partial: E1 already acts as an OOD split. Leave-one-source-out and worst-group reporting are new.
evidence: R: 10 datasets; standard training gives clearly lower OOD than ID performance on each, and existing shift methods do not close the gap.
